patch_description: Instead of computing an independent shortest path per destination (which duplicates transfer cost when destinations share route segments), this approach builds a directed Steiner-tree-like multicast structure: it models the problem as a minimum-cost arborescence rooted at src spanning {src} ∪ dsts (approximated with a prune-based MST over the metric closure / or repeated shortest-path grafting). All destinations share overlapping trunk edges, so cost is paid once per shared edge rather than once per destination. Additionally, for edges with very low throughput relative to demand, the algorithm splits a partition's traffic across edge-disjoint parallel paths to balance load and avoid bottleneck costs, and it prunes the final tree of destination-unreachable branches. This should substantially reduce total cost versus per-destination Dijkstra when destinations cluster behind common gateways (typical in multi-cloud topologies where several regions connect through the same backbone hubs).
